answer_text:
Let

\[
S=\frac{a}{c+kb}+\frac{b}{a+kc}+\frac{c}{b+ka}.
\]

Using the Engel form of Cauchy-Schwarz,

\[
S=\sum_{\text{cyc}}\frac{a^2}{a(c+kb)}
\ge \frac{(a+b+c)^2}{a(c+kb)+b(a+kc)+c(b+ka)}.
\]

Now compute the denominator:

\[
\begin{aligned}
a(c+kb)+b(a+kc)+c(b+ka)
&=ac+kab+ab+kbc+bc+kca\\
&=(1+k)(ab+bc+ca).
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus

\[
S\ge \frac{(a+b+c)^2}{(1+k)(ab+bc+ca)}.
\]

Since

\[
(a+b+c)^2\ge 3(ab+bc+ca),
\]

we get

\[
S\ge \frac{3}{1+k}.
\]

For the inequality

\[
S\ge \frac1{2007}
\]

to hold for all positive \(a,b,c\), we need

\[
\frac{3}{1+k}\ge \frac1{2007}.
\]

Solving,

\[
3\cdot 2007\ge 1+k
\]

\[
6021\ge 1+k
\]

\[
k\le 6020.
\]

If \(k>6020\), taking \(a=b=c\) gives

\[
S=\frac{3}{1+k}<\frac1{2007},
\]

so the inequality fails. Therefore the admissible positive constants are \(0<k\le 6020\), and the largest/sharp value is

\[
\boxed{6020}.
\]
